design_differences_named: Record is zlib-compressed canonical compact v2 JSON (design: dictionary-compact body). The 60 closes and every point field are kept; measured 3645 bytes versus 31239 for the v1 line. Compression was needed because the uncompressed compact record measured 12.8 to 12.9 KB (above the 12 KB budget) with a 112 character content_ref.

Table is a rowid table with a (symbol, dataset) primary key, not WITHOUT ROWID, and page_size is 512: WITHOUT ROWID at 4 KB pages measured 1.18x and rowid at 4 KB 1.09x, rowid at 512 B 1.03x to 1.08x file/live; larger pages exceed the 1.1x budget.
last_trade_date and snapshot_dict columns of the design are not used: the digest column is the window digest and the dictionary is inside the compact record.

The window digest includes ingest_run_id (part of every point's lineage), exactly as the journal's prior.points == candidate.points test did; a re-run with a new run id replaces the row, the same window with the same run id writes zero rows.

The compat export runs after a write at most once per MARKET_SNAPSHOT_EXPORT_INTERVAL_SECONDS (runtime default 3600, the constructor default 0 = synchronous, used by tests) from a daemon thread; flush_export() forces it. A background export in the first run of this task held a long read transaction and slowed the writer transaction from 35 ms to 200 to 600 ms; the export now takes a short consistent read of the raw rows and decodes outside it.
synchronous=FULL, auto_vacuum=INCREMENTAL, busy_timeout=2000 as designed; WAL is truncated after each batch with a 40 ms bounded wait.

host_load_caveat: The timing bounds were measured on a shared 12-core worker VM. On a quiet host the run recorded reader process max 67.7 ms, in-process reader thread max 94.7 ms, write transaction max 66 ms (p99 of 22 batches). Three later runs under host load average 14 to 14.4 gave: pass (reader 85/92 ms, txn max 96 ms), fail (reader thread 131 ms, txn max 309 ms) and fail (reader process 164 ms) while a second pytest suite ran in parallel. The bound test is therefore load sensitive around its 100 ms limit; the hosted acceptance run must repeat it on a quiet host. No test was relaxed. Review round 2 (reviewer saw reader thread 102.8 ms 3/3): GIL hold on the ingest path was reduced (time.sleep(0) between keys in the sqlite append read/build phase; compat export materialises rows with periodic yields and fsyncs every 100 rows instead of one ~40 MB fsync). Measured afterwards on the shared VM (load avg ~3): in-process reader thread max 35-88 ms over 9 runs (was 94-104), reader process max 58-62 ms in 8 of 9 runs. Remaining flakiness is a ~450-570 ms single write transaction in some runs (filesystem journal contention with the export/checkpoint fsync on this shared VM) and one reader-process outlier of 129 ms with a normal transaction, i.e. host noise; 6 of 9 isolated runs and the final 5-suite run (103 passed) were green. No bound was relaxed; hosted acceptance must repeat the run on a quiet host. Follow-up still named: scripts/dev_release_artifacts.py flush_export.
